# `Q-16-10` — Engine extension does not declare static claims

> An engine extension decides what it handles at run time instead of
> declaring it in `_extension.yml`, so Quarto must start it to find out.

## What this means

An execution engine has to tell Quarto two things: which *languages* it
runs (`{python}`, `{julia}`, …) and which *file types* it converts
(`.ipynb`, `.py`, …).

There are two ways to answer.

**At run time.** Quarto starts the engine as a subprocess and calls its
`claimsLanguage` / `claimsFile` functions. This is how engines worked in
Quarto 1, and it still works — the engine just has to be running before
Quarto can ask.

**Ahead of time.** The engine writes the answers into its
`_extension.yml`, and Quarto reads them straight from the file. No
subprocess, no questions.

This warning means the engine is using the first approach. Nothing is
broken; the engine will run your code correctly. But Quarto cannot know
whether the engine is needed without starting it, so it pays that cost
for any document that could need an engine — including documents this
engine turns out not to handle.

## How to fix

Add the declarations to the extension's `_extension.yml`:

```yaml
title: My Python Engine
version: 1.0.0
contributes:
  engines:
    - path: dist/my-engine.js
      name: my-engine
      claims:
        python: true
      file-extensions: [".py"]
      claims-files:
        - extension: ".py"
```

Each key answers one question:

- `name` — the engine's runtime name, so Quarto can register it without
  loading the module to ask.
- `claims` — which languages the engine executes.
- `file-extensions` — which file extensions it can handle at all. Used
  as a fast pre-filter.
- `claims-files` — which file extensions it claims *unconditionally*,
  without needing to look inside the file.

An empty value counts as a real answer. If your engine genuinely handles
no files, write `claims-files: []` — that tells Quarto "none", which is
different from not saying anything.

The warning names exactly which of these keys are absent, so you only
need to add the ones it lists.

## If you do not maintain the extension

Report it to the extension's author — the fix belongs in the extension.

You can add the keys to the copy in your project's `_extensions/`
directory as a local workaround, but updating the extension will
overwrite them.

## Why this warns even when the engine is unused

The warning is about the extension's declarations, not about what this
particular render happened to do. Quarto reports it whenever such an
extension is installed, because the cost is a property of the extension:
any document that could need an engine will pay it, and Quarto cannot
tell in advance which documents those are.

Quarto does avoid the cost where it provably cannot apply. A file type
Quarto owns natively — `.qmd`, `.md`, `.markdown` — is never offered to
an engine at all (see [`Q-2-51`](../markdown/Q-2-51.qmd)), so a project
of plain markdown starts no engine even with such an extension
installed. The warning still appears, because installing the extension
is what needs fixing, not that particular render.
